newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada likely to exceed Q3 lumber export quotas.
newsitem.headline: Canada likely to exceed Q3 lumber export quotas.

text.p: Canada is likely to exceed third quarter limits on softwood lumber exports to the United States, after which shipments would be slapped with an export fee, a government official said on Tuesday.

"(It) very well may be," Ronald McDonald, parliamentary secretary to International Trade Minister Art Eggleton told reporters when asked about the possibility of exceeding quotas for the third (October - December) quarter.

"I would suspect that we will reach it (the limit) and that some companies will exceed their quarterly allocation," McDonald said. "The industry as a whole may exceed the industry quarterly allocation."

McDonald also said that under a provision of the lumber export agreement between Ottawa and Washington, which became effective on April 1, he expected that companies could use 50- 100 million board feet of their quotas for future years.
Canadian lumber exports which exceed 14.7 billion board feet annually or 4.226 billion board feet quarterly are subject to export fees under the five-year agreement.
McDonald said he suspected that 50 to 60 companies would have used or exceeded their quotas for the first two quarters.
"I suspect that pretty much all of them would be in the category, within the restrictions that we have, to apply for a 20 percent drawdown on future quota," he said.
"We anticipate that there could be between 50 and 100 million board feet requested on the draw forward provision that we have on future years," McDonald said.

"We are not sure why that is... Hopefully we'll find that the companies that are in positions where they have expended their quota will be balanced out by companies that will not be expending their quota for the year," McDonald said.
"Most of them are small producers, but if you add it all up, it's still quota that we don't want to lose," he added.

McDonald said soaring lumber prices during the first two quarters of the agreement, have triggered a provision which gives Canada an extra 92 million board feet of duty-free exports for each quarter. He said he hoped the same would occur in the third quarter.

The price above which more duty-free exports are allowed is US$405 dollars for 1,000 board feet on average for quarter. The additional duty-free exports can be used in any of the following four quarters, McDonald said.
He said Canada is most likely to use any additional quotas that become available to give them to so called "new entrants," -- companies which had begun production in 1995 or 1996.

New entrants will be allowed up to 2.0 percent (294 million board feet) of the total annual quota. However, McDonald said he expects new entrants to use only 1.25 percent of the 2.0 percent they are allowed. The remainder, he said, would go to companies drawing down on advance quotas.
Companies who want to draw down on advance quotas have to apply by December 31. He said applications would be processed immediately.
